idea: Bury the product in the middle of the slideshow (not the end, where viewers drop off) so completion requires seeing the ad.

The directive: bury the app mid-slideshow

hook: Bookmark this for S-tier slideshows for your app (SO CHEAP TOO)
body: An exact agent prompt for a 6-slide TikTok photo carousel: slide 1 is a wide candid realistic photo with the hook 5 ways to get [result] in white text; slides 2-6 are genuinely useful numbered tips with specific numbers; exactly ONE middle slide (never first or last) mentions the app in quotes inside its tip, with a photo of a phone in a hand showing the real app screen; every other slide is pure value. Image generation specs (Flux Ultra for faces, nano-banana for consistency, Flux Schnell for cheap b-roll), text safe zones (300px from top, bottom 25% clear of a 1080x1920 frame), and a casual lowercase caption with 4-6 hashtags.
idea: A copy-paste agent prompt that produces the ideal listicle-save carousel: value-dense tips with the product appearing exactly once, in the middle.
sequencing: Slide 1 spec: candid wide photo + hook
Slides 2-6 spec: numbered tips with specific numbers
Image model specs per shot type
formatting: X post with one photo; the post IS the prompt.
why_it_works: Constraints do the work: one middle product mention feels native among pure-value tips; specific numbers and candid visuals earn saves.
what_to_steal: Adapt the prompt verbatim for Louise Carter: 5 ways to keep jewelry from tarnishing with the product on one middle slide, candid iPhone-style visuals, same safe zones.

product: unnamed recipe app (case study; ~$10k MRR claimed)
hook: nah this is actually insane / the account has posts sitting at 40m views
body: Recipe slideshows (one meal per slide) hit 40M views and the app does ~$10k MRR off it: recipes are the most natural slideshow format -- one meal per slide, people save on instinct -- and the app is just all of this, in your pocket. The directive: give away a small piece of what your app does in every slideshow; the app sells the full version.
idea: The sample-then-full-version model: each slideshow gives away one usable piece of the product's value, and the app sells the complete collection.
sequencing: Why recipes work: one meal per slide, saved on instinct
The product as the full version (all of this, in your pocket)
The directive: give away a piece, sell the full version
why_it_works: Save-bait listicles create a collection habit; each save is a micro-commitment that makes the full-version pitch (the app) feel like unlocking what they already started.
what_to_steal: Louise Carter version: styling slideshows (one outfit per slide, save-bait) where the full collection/shop is the pocket version -- give away the styling, sell the pieces.
